examples.en: This company only makes high-quality products.
It's much clearer in high-quality video.
It's expensive, but I'm satisfied because it's high quality.
The taste is different because they use high-quality ingredients.
I saw an ad promising high-quality service.
Farmers work hard to grow high-quality rice.

explain: '고품질 제품', '고품질 서비스'처럼 뒤에 명사가 와요. 반대는 '저품질'이에요. 말할 때는 '품질이 좋다'가 더 자연스럽고, 고품질은 광고나 설명 글에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: A noun follows it: 고품질 제품, 고품질 서비스. The opposite is 저품질. In speech 품질이 좋다 sounds more natural; 고품질 mostly shows up in ads and descriptions.

examples.en: Please sit with your back straight.
If you follow the straight road, you will reach the school.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 마음이 곧발라서 거짓말을 못 해요.
examples.en: That child is so upright that he can't tell a lie.

examples.ko: 자세가 곧바르면 키도 더 커 보여요.
examples.en: If your posture is straight, you also look taller.

examples.ko: 곧발라 보이는 나무를 골라서 기둥으로 썼어요.
examples.en: We picked a tree that looked straight and used it as a pillar.
I promised my parents that I will live honestly from now on.

explain: 몸이나 물건이 굽지 않은 모습, 그리고 마음이 정직한 것에 모두 써요. '르' 불규칙이라 '곧발라요', '곧바른'으로 바뀌어요. 말할 때는 '곧게', '똑바로'처럼 말하는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: It describes things that are not bent and also a person with an honest heart. It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '곧발라요' and '곧바른'. In speech many people say '곧게' or '똑바로' instead.

examples.ko: 힘든 일이 많았지만 그는 꿋꿋이 버텼어요.
examples.en: There was a lot of hardship, but he held out firmly.

examples.ko: 비바람 속에서도 나무가 꿋꿋이 서 있어요.
examples.en: The tree stands firm even in wind and rain.

examples.ko: 친구들이 놀려도 꿋꿋이 제 길을 갔어요.
examples.en: Even when friends teased him, he kept going his own way.
Grandmother keeps running the shop bravely, even on her own.
Even if you fail, try again with a strong heart.

examples.ko: 아이는 아파도 울지 않고 꿋꿋이 웃었어요.
examples.en: The child didn't cry even though it hurt, and smiled bravely.

explain: 어려운 일이 있어도 마음이 약해지지 않고 버티는 모습에 써요. 형용사 '꿋꿋하다'에서 나온 말이라 '꿋꿋한 사람'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes someone who stays strong and does not give in despite hardship. It comes from the adjective '꿋꿋하다', so you can also say '꿋꿋한 사람' (a resilient person).

examples.en: I solved the problem easily, so I felt good.
Thanks to the directions, I found the place easily.

examples.ko: 준비를 미리 하면 수월히 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you prepare in advance, you can finish smoothly.
I thought it would be settled easily, but it wasn't.
I'm glad the child fell asleep without trouble.

examples.ko: 이 앱을 쓰면 수월히 예약할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use this app, you can book easily.

explain: '수월하게'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 보통 '수월하게'나 '쉽게'를 더 많이 써요. '수월히'는 글에서 자연스러워요. 반대는 '힘들게'나 '어렵게'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '수월하게', and in speech people usually say '수월하게' or '쉽게' more. '수월히' sounds natural in writing. The opposite would be '힘들게' or '어렵게'.

examples.en: This job is not just difficult, it's extremely difficult.
It's hard to pass with only an ordinary amount of effort.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 여간해서는 화를 내지 않아요.
examples.en: He hardly ever gets angry.

examples.ko: 아이를 혼자 키우는 게 여간 힘든 일이 아니에요.
examples.en: Raising a child alone is no easy thing at all.

examples.ko: 이렇게 도와주셔서 여간 고마운 게 아니에요.
examples.en: I can't tell you how grateful I am for your help.

examples.ko: 오늘은 여간 덥지 않아서 밖에 나가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's so hot today that it's hard to go outside.

explain: 거의 항상 부정 표현과 붙어 나와요. '여간 힘들지 않아요'는 모양은 부정인데 '무척 힘들어요'를 강하게 말해요. '여간해서는 화를 안 내요'처럼 쓰면 '웬만해서는'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It almost always comes with a negative. '여간 힘들지 않아요' looks negative but strongly means 'it's really hard'. In '여간해서는 화를 안 내요' it can be swapped with '웬만해서는' (hardly ever).

examples.en: The corner of this paper is a right angle.
The two lines meet at a right angle.
I placed the desk at a right angle to the wall.
I drew a right angle with a set square.

examples.ko: 길이 갑자기 직각으로 꺾여서 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: The road turned sharply at a right angle, and I got lost.
Find the area of the right triangle.

explain: 90도가 직각이고, 90도보다 작으면 예각, 크면 둔각이에요. 길이나 선이 딱 꺾일 때도 '직각으로 꺾이다'라고 해요. 보통 '직각으로' 또는 '직각 삼각형'처럼 붙여서 써요.
explain_en: 90 degrees is a right angle, smaller is '예각', and larger is '둔각'. A road or line that bends sharply can also '직각으로 꺾이다'. It usually appears as '직각으로' or '직각 삼각형'.
